senses.gloss:
Tauvilikā, occurring once in a hymn of the Atharvaveda, is a word of quite uncertain sense. Roth thinks it means some kind of beast; Zimmer and Whitney regard it as a sort of plant; Sāyaṇa explains it as a disease-causing demon, while Bloomfield leaves the sense doubtful.
Foot notes vi. 16, 3.

Altindisches Leben, 72.
